Define a fishery

Source: R/spec_fishery.R
fishery.Rd

A fishery is a set of fleets that share a time horizon. Each fleet has a nominal effort trend, process noise on effort that is common to all species (so species caught by the same fleet share effort anomalies) and an optional annual efficiency increase (effort creep) that raises fishing mortality but is not visible in the nominal effort index.

Usage

fishery(
  fleets,
  years,
  trends,
  sigmaE = 0.15,
  creep = 0,
  creep_start = NULL,
  name = "fishery",
  seed = 123
)

validate_fishery(x)

fishery_years(x)

Arguments

fleets

character vector of fleet names.

years

integer vector of years (first year = unfished start).

trends

named list of effort_trend() objects, one per fleet.

sigmaE

lognormal SD of the effort process noise (shared across species); scalar or one value per fleet.

creep

annual efficiency increase per fleet (0.02 = 2% per year).

creep_start

first year of creep per fleet (default: first year).

name

a label.

seed

seed for the effort realisation; every species built with this fishery sees the same effort.

x

a floss_fishery.

Value

a list of class floss_fishery.

Details

Fishing mortality of species \(s\) by fleet \(f\) in year \(y\) is $$F_{s,f,y} = q_{s,f}\,\eta_{f,y}\,E_{f,y},\quad \eta_{f,y} = (1 + c_f)^{\max(0,\,y - y^{c}_f)},$$ where \(E\) is nominal effort (trend x lognormal noise), \(c_f\) the creep rate and \(q_{s,f}\) the species catchability, set in species() as relative catchability x \(F_{MSY}\).

Examples

fishery(fleets = c("traps", "linefish"), years = 1980:2025,
        trends = list(traps = effort_trend(fhi = 1, flo = 0.8),
                      linefish = effort_trend(fhi = 2, flo = 1)))
#> FLOSS fishery 'fishery': 2 fleets, 1980-2025
#>     fleet                                        trend sigmaE creep creep_start
#>     traps fudc(e0=0.05, hi=1, lo=0.8, breaks=0.5/0.75)   0.15     0        1980
#>  linefish   fudc(e0=0.05, hi=2, lo=1, breaks=0.5/0.75)   0.15     0        1980
